lead: South Dakota homes face river floods, hail and long, hard winters. DryFlare helps owners from Sioux Falls to Rapid City get water out and dry quickly.
risk: river and flash flooding, hail and frozen pipes
why: In June 2024, heavy rain flooded the Big Sioux River. Homes in North Sioux City and around McCook Lake were damaged or destroyed. Rapid City still remembers the 1972 Rapid Creek flood, which killed more than 200 people. FEMA has declared 43 water and storm disasters in South Dakota since 2000.

Severe storms bring big hail to Sioux Falls and the eastern plains. Winter cold freezes pipes in homes and ranch buildings. Spring melt can push the Missouri, James and Big Sioux rivers into towns. North Dakota, Iowa and Nebraska share these risks.
image_alt: Worker drilling into a new drywall panel
image_caption: Homes reached by South Dakota river floods often need new drywall once the framing is dry.
problems: Big Sioux, James and Missouri river towns
Sioux Falls and eastern South Dakota
tips: Buy flood insurance well before spring melt.
Have your roof checked after hail.
Keep snow piles away from the foundation.
insurance: Overland flooding is not covered by South Dakota homeowners policies; only flood insurance covers it.

faq.q: How do I dry out a flooded basement in South Dakota?
faq.a: Pump out standing water, then remove wet carpet and drywall. Run commercial dehumidifiers and air movers until moisture readings are normal. Concrete walls and floors can take several days to dry.

licensing: South Dakota has no statewide general contractor license. Sioux Falls and Rapid City license some contractors locally. Plumbers and electricians need state licenses.
